hints: Notice the hinge at Y carries the $4.0\times 10^4\text{ N}$ weight downward and is pushed by two symmetric beams each at $50^{\circ}$ to the horizontal.
Each beam force $F$ acts along the beam, so its upward vertical part is $F\sin50^{\circ}$ because $50^{\circ}$ is measured from the horizontal.
For vertical equilibrium the two upward components must balance the weight, so set $2F\sin50^{\circ}=4.0\times 10^4\text{ N}$ and solve for $F$.
walkthrough: Consider point Y: forces are the $4.0\times 10^4\text{ N}$ weight downward plus a force $F$ from each steel beam directed along the beam away from the beam.
By symmetry the left and right beam forces have equal magnitude $F$. Each beam makes $50^{\circ}$ with the horizontal, so the angle to the vertical is $40^{\circ}$.
Resolve vertically: each beam contributes $F\sin50^{\circ}$ upward, while horizontal components $F\cos50^{\circ}$ cancel left-right.
Equilibrium in the vertical direction requires resultant force zero: $2F\sin50^{\circ} - 4.0\times 10^4\text{ N} = 0$.
